old: A very long run of bahuvrīhi adjectives (all nom./acc. sg.), joined in the print without spaces, in the style of a description of a desirable body. No noun is stated in this unit; the later units (to u136, where 'śarīram' stands) appear to continue the same description. GROUPING: appears to continue into u119 (same construction). Scope doubts: whether mahā 'large' applies to every member of its compound (head ... voice), whether upacita applies to all of 'thigh ... palate', whether dīrgha applies to every member of its compound, and what 'both qualities' (ubhaya-guṇa) refers to, are not settled by the Sanskrit; translated in the most literal way. 'stanāgra' = breast-tip (probable: nipple). 'karṇa-pīṭha' is literally ear-seat; the exact part is unclear. 'jatru' = collarbone region (probable). 'pṛṣṭha-vaṃśa' = spine (probable). 'meḍhra' = penis (standard). 'adhara-oṣṭha' taken as one item 'lower lip'; it could be two items (lower lip, lip). 'ātāmra' = reddish. 'netrānta' = corners/ends of the eyes. 'caṅkramaṇa' = walking, gait; 'nīcair baddha' = set low. 'citta' is printed 'mind' among body parts and is probably a misprint (not corrected). 'sauhārda' = friendliness, goodwill. Printed 'ucchāsa' conjecturally read as ucchvāsa (breath). Three stretches are unreadable and kept unsplit (tvakacakarajana; śuklaśukaṃmaṃḍaladaśanacarita; vaṃtāṃguli); translations leave them 'unclear' and give no meaning. Low confidence throughout.
